description:
FILED s473t4 (#1501 CHECK 2 round 1, 2026-09-13).  docs/not-supported.md "String eval with multiple package sections" says "The single-switch shape (`package X;` plus a body) is supported and common".  It is -- but only for the two plainest spellings.  MEASURED (probe, perl 5.40.3 accepts all seven):

    eval 'package Foo; 1'          perl: none   pcl: none
    eval 'package Foo;'            perl: none   pcl: none
    eval 'package Foo 1.2; 1'      perl: none   pcl: PCL: unsupported in string eval: multiple package sections
    eval 'package Foo2 1.2;'       perl: none   pcl: same refusal
    eval 'package Foo3 1.2'        perl: none   pcl: same refusal
    eval 'package Foo4 { 1 }'      perl: none   pcl: same refusal
    eval 'package Foo5 1.2 { 1 }'  perl: none   pcl: same refusal

THE SITE is Pl/Parser2.pm's eval-collapse guard, which reads

    && $segments[1]{pkg_stmt} && !$segments[1]{blockform}
    && !defined $segments[1]{version}

(and the same two exclusions in the four-segment bare-block arm below it).  Neither exclusion is a multi-switch: a `package NAME VERSION;` is ONE switch that also sets $VERSION, and a `package NAME BLOCK` is not a switch at all -- it is self-contained and the code after it is back in the outer package.

BEHIND IT: t/op/packagev.t's 109 diverging rows (the file's whole method is `eval "package withversion 1.2"` in six spellings and then asserting `$@ eq ''`), t/op/inccode-tie.t's 89-row shortfall, and t/uni/opcroak.t.

NOT taken in t4 because it is the #226 / E4.1 eval-collapse machinery and the bar was "no new mechanism": the collapse would have to carry the version to the region's $VERSION assignment and, for the block form, keep the block's own scope.  Both are bounded, and the probe above is the acceptance table.  Round t5b.

=== DONE (s484a) ===

SHIPPED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13).  NEITHER exclusion was a second switch, and
perl accepts all seven spellings with `$@` empty -- the acceptance table in
this task, re-probed as scratch/s484a/probes/p1587.pl (19 rows).

THE VERSION (arm A, the 2-segment collapse).  `package NAME VERSION;` is ONE
switch that also sets $VERSION, so `!defined $segments[1]{version}` is gone and
the version rides on the collapsed region as `version`/`version_pkg`/
`version_stmt`.  The cell must be spelled for X, NOT for the section: the
region's own package is the eval's ROOT, so a section-spelled cell would have
been `$main::VERSION`.

THE EMISSION BECAME ONE READING, `_pkg_version_forms`, called by the file-mode
assembler (`_assemble`) and the eval-mode one (`_assemble_eval_mode`) at the
same phase position.  A second copy would have been a second chance to
disagree about the PHASE, which is the one thing s437 had to fix -- and the
phase is observable: `eval 'package V 1.5; BEGIN { $seen = $V::VERSION } 1'`
now reads 1.5 from the BEGIN.

THE BLOCK FORM (arm B, new, 3 segments) NEEDED NO NEW MECHANISM.  PPI's
segments are [leading | X's block | back to the caller's package], and
`_lower_block`'s `if ($blk)` arm -- the arm a nested `package X { ... }`
already takes in FILE mode -- emits enter / body / restore / remainder with
exactly perl's scoping (the code after the block is back in the outer package:
`eval 'package Foo { our $x = 1 } our $x = 7; $x'` is 7 and `$Foo::x` is 1).
So the collapse hands the Package statement ITSELF back into one region
segment and that arm runs.  The three-segment shape is the ONLY one accepted:
two blocks make FIVE segments and stay refused, which keeps
`eval 'package A { } package B { }'` a multi-switch.

THE BLOCK FORM'S TAIL VALUE was wrong on BOTH paths, and it is the same bug in
file mode: the restore call's value is the package NAME and it was the last
form, so `eval 'package X { 42 }'` answered "main" and, outside eval mode,
`sub f { package T { 42 } }` returned "main" too.  When a value is wanted and
nothing follows the block, the restore goes behind a `prog1`.  Four FILE-mode
shapes move to perl's answer (probe b1587.pl: 42 / undef / 6 / T5, all "main"
before), and corpus-diff is still IDENTICAL because no corpus file has the
shape.

ONE PREDICATE `_seg_is_pkg_switch` answers "is this segment a statement-form
package switch" for all four askers, because a blockform segment now carries
`pkg_stmt` too (it has one) while NOT being a switch.

THE `Parser2 TODO: versioned nested package statement` REFUSAL STAYS for a
genuinely nested versioned switch (`sub f { package X 1.2; ... }`) -- nothing
there would set $VERSION and dropping it silently is the #138 failure mode --
and exempts exactly the statement whose SECTION emits it, derived from the
same field (`_eval_version_stmt`, set once per segment in `_lower_segments`
from `$seg->{version_stmt}`).

BARS on the rebased tree (base 8c8fa4c0, generation v2-1340, artifacts
regenerated -- stamp-only diffs):
  * corpus-diff 8c8fa4c0: emission IDENTICAL across 111 files, silent drops 5
    unchanged, 6 shapes identical
  * emission-ab --shapes --list lib/**: 27 files SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF
  * gate-set-scan over BOTH populations: 638 files IDENTICAL
  * probe: all seven spellings accepted, $VERSION readable after each,
    __PACKAGE__ right inside AND after the block, a sub in the block callable
    as Blk::f, unqualified globals resolving in the region (`our` and
    undeclared), a v-string version accepted, and the multi-switch + two-block
    shapes STILL refused
  * guard `Pl/t/parser2-02.t` 147 -> 159; rows 54-61 FAIL on a `2ffefb36`
    archive extraction and 62-65 abort it
  * docs/not-supported.md "String eval with multiple package sections" now
    lists all seven spellings and says why a VERSION and a BLOCK are not
    switches

FILED, both PRE-EXISTING and found by the acceptance probe:
  * #1640 -- `package Foo v1.2.3` stores $VERSION as the literal TEXT, so
    `sprintf "%vd"` prints the source characters (118.49.46.50.46.51).
    Pre-existing in FILE mode, measured on the base tree.
  * #1641 -- `eval 'package Foo;'` answers the package NAME where perl answers
    undef.  Pre-existing for the plain spelling; the fix made it uniform
    across all three statement spellings rather than uniform across one.

--- ADDENDUM (same session, found by the COMPANION LEG) ---

op/cproto.t and op/packagev.t moved as predicted, but op/inccode-tie.t and
uni/opcroak.t did NOT: their shape is a BLOCK-form package inside a BARE
BLOCK, which the T-A1 flattening renders as FIVE segments where the top-level
spelling is three.  Arm B is therefore keyed on the STRUCTURE, not on a count
(a count-keyed arm would have had to be written twice for one rule): exactly
one package-affecting segment and it is a BLOCKFORM, no statement-form switch
anywhere, every other segment the eval's root.  The s353 whitelists then apply
for their own reason and only where it holds: flattening ERASES the bare
block's scope, so the literal-only TAIL rule is kept for exactly that case
while a top-level block form may be followed by anything.

MEASURED after it: op/cproto.t 71/183 -> 254/0 OK, op/packagev.t 198/109 ->
228/79, uni/opcroak.t's `aborted-forms` note gone (the eval RUNS; its 5 rows
fail on their own subject, UTF-8 error-message text, which had never been
measured because nothing got that far).  op/inccode-tie.t is STILL refused --
its `push @INC, ...` tail is not literal-only -- and that residue is #1642,
which carries the reproducer, why the rule is conservative for a block form,
and what the bar would be.
subject: `eval "package NAME VERSION"` and `eval "package NAME { â¦ }"` are refused as "multiple package sections" -- the #226 single-switch collapse excludes exactly those two spellings (op/packagev.t 109 rows + op/inccode-tie.t 89)
